memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head. Bring his sons and dress them in tunics and fasten caps on them. Then tie sashes on Aaron and his sons. The priesthood is theirs by a lasting ordinance. Then you shall ordain Aaron and his sons." - Exodus 29:7-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Oil is poured over Aaron's head — not sprinkled or dabbed, but poured. Anointing marked a person as chosen and equipped by God for a particular calling. It was visible, generous, and unmistakable. Everyone watching knew that this man had been designated by God.

Anointing throughout Scripture signifies being commissioned and empowered for God's purposes. Kings were anointed, prophets were anointed, priests were anointed. The word "Messiah" itself means "anointed one" — and Jesus is the fulfilment of all three offices, our anointed Prophet, Priest, and King.

Remarkably, John writes to ordinary believers that they have an anointing from the Holy One (1 John 2:20, 27). Through the Spirit, God has designated and equipped you for the purposes He has for your life. You may not feel especially chosen or capable. Aaron probably did not either, standing there with oil running down his face. But God does not call people because they are equipped; He equips the people He calls. Whatever God has set before you, He has also given you what you need for it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I believe God has equipped me for what He has called me to?
Where am I holding back because I feel unqualified?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You do not call the equipped — You equip the called. Thank You for Your Spirit at work in me. Give me confidence to step into what You have set before me. Amen.
